items.scene: After class, a student jokes with her professor and asks whether she may turn in the paper two days late.
items.question: What role structure best describes the interaction?
items.why_this_case_matters: Friendly tone does not remove the professor's formal academic authority.

items.scene: A nurse tells a patient how to take the prescribed medicine and checks whether the patient has questions.
items.question: Which role structure matters most?
items.why_this_case_matters: This is a clear expert-to-dependent care relationship.

items.scene: At a meeting, an older attendee speaks confidently and tells a junior analyst to change the slides, but the attendee has no official title in the team.
items.question: What role structure is most defensible?
options: Peer or unclear, with no formal authority shown
items.why_this_case_matters: This tests a likely shortcut: do not infer authority from age or confidence alone.

items.scene: A teacher asks a student to help restart the classroom projector before class.
items.question: What should the student say to avoid seeming disrespectful?
options: The teacher/student hierarchy is the main issue
The student should give a tactful reply
This is a communication-strategy question, not role diagnosis
items.why_this_case_matters: This is a boundary case because it asks what to say, not what role structure exists.
